title: DAVE's safety interlock (the guard extension)
description: Rules that .pi/extensions/guard/index.ts checks before every tool call. Gives VS Code autocomplete and hover help for .pi/guard.jsonc.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Ask you first: Yes once, Yes for the rest of this session, or No.
Block it. You can't approve it from pi.
Send it to the judge model, which answers allow, ask or never. Needs `judge.url`.

command.markdownDescription: Shell commands, matched by their first word (`rm` also catches `/bin/rm` and `sudo rm`). More words must come later in the same command, in order: `git push`. `*` matches anything inside one word: `curl --data*`.

file.markdownDescription: A name with no `/` (`.env`, `*.pem`) matches that file or folder anywhere. A path (`notes/private`) is relative to this folder and covers everything inside it. `~/` is your home folder.

access.markdownDescription: For `file` rules: `write` (the default) covers write and edit, `read` covers read, grep, find and ls, `any` covers both.

tool.markdownDescription: A tool by name, such as `bash`, `write`, or an MCP tool like `export_ics`. `*` works here too.

why.markdownDescription: Finishes the sentence "DAVE wants to ..." when the guard asks or blocks.

exact.markdownDescription: For `command` rules: the whole command line must be exactly this text (spaces squeezed). "Always allow" in the guard's question saves rules like this.

note.markdownDescription: Shown to the person when the rule asks or blocks, in your own words. In a classroom file, the teacher's note: `Ask me before adding packages.`

dial.description: What happens when no rule matches.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Ask before every tool call, even reading a file.
Ask before shell commands, file edits and MCP tools that aren't read-only.
"ask" rules are skipped. "never" rules still block.

rules.description: A "never" rule always wins. Otherwise rules are checked top to bottom and the first match decides.

classroom.markdownDescription: Path to a teacher's classroom file, relative to this folder. Its rules apply on top of yours, and the stricter answer wins. `/guard lesson` switches between its lessons.

outsideThisFolder.description: Writing or editing a file outside this folder.

destructiveTools.description: MCP tools whose server marks them as destructive.

noOneToAsk.description: What "ask" becomes when nobody can answer: print mode, or a crew worker.

audit.description: The guard records every tool call, its verdict and the rules in force to an audit file on this computer. /guard audit shows it.

keepDays.description: Days to keep each session's audit file. Older files are deleted when a session starts.

otherCommands.description: Shell commands no rule matched. Leave out to let the dial decide; "check" sends them to the judge.

judge.description: How the decision model judges "check" calls. Its connection is usually set with /guard judge setup, outside the repo.

url.markdownDescription: Pins a judge for this project, winning over the connection saved by `/guard judge setup` in `~/.pi/agent/guard-judge.json`. A System One endpoint such as Ollama, e.g. `http://localhost:11434`. The guard calls `<url>/v1/systemone`.

model.description: A System One model Ollama serves: clef:27b, clef-flash ...

apiKey.markdownDescription: Bearer key, only if needed. `$NAME` reads an environment variable.

allowAt.description: The judge's allow counts only at this probability or higher; otherwise the guard asks you.

timeoutMs.description: How long the judge gets to answer once its model is loaded, in ms.

coldStartMs.description: How long the judge gets when its model has to load first: the first call, or the first after 30 idle minutes. Never shorter than timeoutMs.

ifUnavailable.description: What happens when the judge can't be reached or is too slow.

markdownEnumDescriptions: The judge's `never` becomes a question for you. It can flag a call as dangerous, but you decide.
maxVerdict.markdownDescription: The strictest answer the judge may give. Applied by the guard after the judge answers, so it holds whatever the model does. Explicit `never` rules are separate and still block.
